correctness.rationale: Noe (2006) Eq. (13) gives exactly the base-seven digit language. In the new proof the six carries for u+jd are updated by exact integer quotient and remainder and the final zero state is equivalent to all six terms lying below the cutoff. All 49 column choices per state are enumerated; the 24-state matrix is finite and closed. The supplied standalone exact-arithmetic checker proves the full characteristic-polynomial and rational-function identity using Cayley--Hamilton, then subtracts precisely 6^r zero-step assignments. Direct enumeration of r=0..3 and independent trinomial checks through n=149 agree, without substituting finite observations for proof.

originality.rationale: The new item is strictly the explicit all-spacing rational generating function for six-term maximal progressions in the modulo-seven central-trinomial support. Its digit criterion is already Noe (2006); maximal length six is already covered by Walker--Walker (2018); and finite-state methods preexist in Rowland--Yassawi (2013). Inspected primary claims and actual mathematical-index searches did not produce the evaluated all-step frequency or a stronger theorem yielding these specific coefficients. Historical priority is therefore qualified, not certified.
residual_risks: A general unpublished or uninspected digit-set enumeration theorem may already contain this exact specialization.

value.rationale: Maximal-length arithmetic progression count at every base-seven scale is a natural additive invariant of a classical nondivisibility support, motivated before calculation by the known sharp length bound. The all-spacing degree-eight rational census distinguishes nine progressions at depth two from 265 at depth three and establishes a complete infinite pattern, not a chosen finite slice. Neither the upper bound nor the density of permitted digits determines it.
